citation: Barry, Robert J., Adam R. Clarke, Stuart J. Johnstone, Christopher A. Magee, and Jacqueline A. Rushby. "EEG Differences Between Eyes-Closed and Eyes-Open Resting Conditions." Clinical Neurophysiology 118, no. 12 (2007): 2765-2773. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinph.2007.07.028.
discipline: clinical neurophysiology / psychophysiology; EEG-methodology study of arousal vs. activation in resting-state baselines
thesis: Using simultaneous EEG (delta/theta/alpha/beta absolute power, 9 scalp regions) and skin conductance level (SCL) recording across alternating 2-min eyes-closed/eyes-open resting blocks in 28 university students, the authors show that the well-known eyes-closed-to-eyes-open reduction in EEG power is not a single undifferentiated process: alpha power falls globally and uniformly (tracking SCL, indexing arousal), while delta, theta, and beta show topographically-focal changes (indexing separable, stimulus/processing-related activation). The paper concludes eyes-closed and eyes-open are not equivalent EEG baselines and recommends eyes-closed as the default arousal baseline and eyes-open as the default activation baseline for tasks involving visual processing or fixation. The paper does not discuss boredom; it is included in this cluster as normative EEG-baseline-methodology background for the strand's boredom-EEG studies and the not-yet-built dataset entry's EEG channel.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.summary: Structured abstract (objective/methods/results/conclusions/significance) previewing the arousal/activation distinction and the recommendation that eyes-closed and eyes-open are non-equivalent resting baselines.

sections.title: 1. Introduction
sections.summary: Reviews classic alpha-desynchronization literature (Berger 1933; Adrian and Matthews 1934; Jasper 1936; Smith 1938) and its two rival mechanistic accounts (Reticular Activating System mediation vs. widespread thalamo-cortical communication); introduces the arousal/activation distinction (Pribram and McGuinness, 1975) as operationalized in the authors' prior work (Barry et al. 2004, 2005a, 2005b; VaezMousavi et al. 2007); notes no prior study examined EEG topography (vs. mean power) across eyes-closed/eyes-open, or bands beyond alpha; states aim and hypotheses.

sections.title: 2. Method
sections.summary: 2.1 Participants (28 university students); 2.2 Physiological recording (SCL + 19-site EEG per 10-20 system); 2.3 Procedure (32 min alternating 2-min eyes-closed/eyes-open blocks, tone-cued, 'triplet' averaging design); 2.4 Data extraction (FFT absolute power, 4 bands, 2-s epochs); 2.5 Statistical analyses (correlations; repeated-measures ANOVA; 3-way topographic condition x sagittal x lateral ANOVA with vector-scaling control).

sections.title: 3. Results
sections.summary: 3.1 Identification of EEG arousal measure(s) -- SCL-alpha correlations across eyes-closed periods; 3.2 Differences in means between conditions -- SCL and across-scalp band power; 3.3 Topographic EEG effects of condition -- delta, theta, alpha, beta each analyzed; 3.4 Confirmation of alpha as an EEG arousal measure -- alpha change-score x SCL change-score correlation.

sections.title: 4. Discussion
sections.summary: Interprets alpha as a pure global arousal marker and topographically-focal delta/theta/beta changes as activation/processing markers; relates findings to the RAS-mediation vs. thalamo-cortical-communication debate on alpha desynchronization; issues the central methodological recommendation on baseline choice, applied explicitly to ERP paradigms using visual fixation points.

sections.title: Acknowledgements and References
sections.summary: Australian Research Council Discovery funding acknowledgement; full reference list including the authors' own prior arousal/activation studies.

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: treated only by loose analogy, never the authors' own framing: the eyes-open visual-fixation/processing condition parallels an 'engaged' state relative to passive eyes-closed rest, but the source frames this exclusively in arousal/activation terms and never invokes engagement, flow, or boredom

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: treated only by loose analogy: eyes-closed rest (no external target, no visual-processing demand) is the paper's closest physiological analogue to reduced external engagement; offered here to meet this strand's mandatory construct-treatment requirement honestly, not to claim the source addresses attention lapses or mind-wandering

measures.label: EEG eyes-open vs. eyes-closed
measures.signal: continuous scalp EEG, 19 sites (Fp1, Fp2, F7, F3, Fz, F4, F8, T3, C3, Cz, C4, T4, T5, P3, Pz, P4, T6, O1, O2), International 10-20 system, linked-ears reference
measures.apparatus: electrode cap with tin electrodes; amplification EEG x20,000 / EOG x5,000; bandpass 0-30 Hz; 16-bit A/D at 512 Hz; impedance <5 kOhm; 32 min of alternating 2-min eyes-closed/eyes-open blocks cued by a 1000 Hz tone; 'triplet' averaging design (first 3 and last 3 blocks) to control order/time effects
measures.key_result: significant across-scalp power reductions in all 4 bands from eyes-closed to eyes-open (delta F=46.47, theta F=23.42, alpha F=15.12, beta F=8.71, all p<.01-.001); only alpha showed a uniform reduction with no topographic (condition x region) interaction, confirming the eyes-closed/eyes-open manipulation dissociates a global arousal component from focal activation components

measures.label: EEG alpha/theta power
measures.signal: absolute power (FFT, 10% Welch window, 2-s epochs) in theta (4-7.5 Hz) and alpha (8-13 Hz) bands, per electrode, per condition
measures.apparatus: same 19-site recording setup as above; power averaged into 9 topographic regions (left/midline/right x frontal/central/posterior) for the 3-way ANOVA
measures.key_result: alpha = confirmed global arousal marker: ~40% reduction eyes-closed to eyes-open, uniform across all sites, correlating negatively with SCL (r=-.37, -.36, -.11 across the three eyes-closed periods; r=-.32 for the eyes-closed-to-eyes-open change score); theta = activation marker: significant global reduction that was significantly larger in posterior regions (condition x F

measures.label: heart rate / HRV (+ skin conductance, unlisted sub-type)
measures.apparatus: Ag/AgCl disk electrodes on ventral surfaces of digits II and III of the non-dominant hand; 0.05 M NaCl inert ointment base; constant 0.5 V applied
measures.key_result: SCL increased significantly from eyes-closed to eyes-open (F=5.53, p<.05, with a marginal decline over time, F=3.35, p=.078); negatively correlated with mean alpha at the first (r=-.37, p=.032) and second (r=-.36, p=.035) eyes-closed periods and with the alpha eyes-closed-to-eyes-open change score (r=-.32, p=.047), the paper's operational confirmation of the SCL-alpha arousal linkage

measures.label: EEG frontal alpha asymmetry
measures.signal: not operationalized as a dedicated laterality/asymmetry index in this paper
measures.key_result: not treated: alpha's topography (posterior-dominant, slight right lateralization) showed no condition interaction, so this study offers no direct frontal-asymmetry-baseline finding; flagged as a relevant methodological gap for bor-sec-30 (Perone et al.), which studies frontal EEG asymmetry across a boring task and must independently justify its baseline choice

measures.label: EEG functional connectivity
measures.key_result: not treated: no coherence/connectivity analysis is reported; flagged as a relevant methodological gap for bor-sec-33 (Yuvaraj et al.), which studies EEG functional connectivity during boredom and must independently justify its baseline choice

readings.claim: Eyes-closed SCL correlated negatively with mean alpha power at the first (r=-.37, p=.032) and second (r=-.36, p=.035) eyes-closed periods, replicating the authors' previously reported inverse SCL-alpha arousal linkage on a between-subjects basis; the correlation, though still negative, was not significant by the third period (r=-.11).

SCL increased significantly from eyes-closed to eyes-open (F=5.53, p<.05), and all four EEG bands (delta, theta, alpha, beta) showed significant across-scalp mean power reductions eyes-closed to eyes-open, with no time effects or condition-by-time interactions.

Delta and theta reductions were significantly larger in specific regions (delta: frontal, midline/right-hemisphere-central; theta: posterior) rather than uniform across the scalp -- focal, activation-consistent changes superimposed on the global reduction.

Alpha's ~40% reduction from eyes-closed to eyes-open was essentially uniform at every site, with no significant condition-by-topography interaction surviving vector scaling -- consistent with alpha indexing a purely global, non-regional process (arousal).

Beta showed the most complex pattern: significant posterior/right-hemisphere reduction accompanied by a small but reliable increase in left frontal regions, so the net across-scalp beta reduction masks opposite-signed focal effects and should not be read as a simple global decrease.
The change in alpha power from eyes-closed to eyes-open correlated negatively with the corresponding change in SCL (r=-.32, one-tailed p=.047), confirming alpha as the paper's arousal index.

Alpha indexes global arousal (tracking SCL, spatially uniform) while topographically-focal delta/theta/beta changes index activation (separable, stimulus/processing-related energy mobilization); eyes-closed and eyes-open resting conditions are therefore not equivalent EEG baselines and should be chosen according to whether the target task involves visual processing or a visual fixation point (as in many ERP paradigms).

This study's arousal/activation decomposition qualifies the classic alpha-desynchronization literature (Berger 1933 onward), which treated visual-stimulation-induced alpha suppression as a single 'cortical activation' phenomenon without distinguishing global-arousal from focal-processing contributions.

tensions.axis: Reticular Activating System (RAS) mediation vs. widespread thalamo-cortical communication as the mechanism of alpha desynchronization to visual input
tensions.note: the paper does not adjudicate this long-standing mechanistic debate directly, but its arousal/activation decomposition offers a partial reframing: the global, SCL-tracking component of alpha reduction is consistent with a RAS-style arousal account, while the topographically-focal delta/theta/beta changes are consistent with the thalamo-cortical processing account, suggesting both mechanisms may operate simultaneously rather than competitively.

tensions.axis: eyes-closed and eyes-open resting conditions as equivalent, interchangeable EEG/ERP baselines (the prior literature's implicit assumption) vs. this paper's finding that they are not equivalent
tensions.note: the paper's central methodological contribution directly contests the common practice (particularly in ERP research using visual fixation points) of treating eyes-open and eyes-closed rest as interchangeable 'lowest-arousal' baselines.

tensions.axis: relative EEG power (used in the authors' earlier child study, Barry et al. 2004, to control for skull/bone-thickness confounds) vs. absolute EEG power (used here, following Barry et al. 2005b)
tensions.note: the authors explicitly justify using absolute power in this adult study because relative-power changes in one band are not independent of other bands and could confound the arousal/activation distinction.

dataset_channels.target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study): EEG eyes-open/eyes-closed baseline channel
dataset_channels.note: This paper's demonstration that eyes-closed and eyes-open resting EEG differ in both global arousal (alpha, SCL) and topographic activation (delta, theta, beta) is the normative methodological citation for how a VR attention study's resting-state EEG baseline channel should be chosen and interpreted, should the not-yet-built dataset entry include one; the dataset entry does not exist on disk, so this bridge documents an intended methodological linkage rather than a confirmed one (P/anticipatory-application).
